title: Quantitative Neuronal Morphometry by Supervised and Unsupervised Learning
author: Bijari, Valera, et al.

steps.title: Install L-Measure software
steps.instruction: Download and install L‑Measure version 5.3 (or version 5.2 if required) for your operating system from the L‑Measure website.

steps.title: Set up Python environment
steps.instruction: Install Python 3.8, then add the required packages: matplotlib 3.3.4, NumPy 1.20.1, Pandas 1.2.2, scikit‑learn 0.24.1, SciPy 1.6.0.

substeps.instruction: Activate a virtual environment in the ‘scripts’ directory and run `pip install -r requirements.txt`.
Or create the conda environment with `conda env create --name star-protocol -f star-protocol.yaml`.
After installation, run scripts via `python script_name.py [input parameters]` or through any preferred Python IDE.

steps.title: Download protocol scripts and data
steps.instruction: Clone or download all Python scripts and representative datasets from the GitLab repository at https://gitlab.orc.gmu.edu/kbijari/zebrafish-analysis-protocol.

steps.title: Obtain reconstruction files
steps.instruction: Use the reconstruction files provided in the GitLab repository or retrieve additional SWC files from NeuroMorpho.Org (Ascoli et al., 2007).

description: Technical details of data acquisition, imaging modalities and neuronal tracing are discussed in depth in the original publication (Valera et al., 2021). Continuous advances in both microscopy and computational power are making the semi-automated reconstructions of neuronal arbors progressively more practical (Peng et al., 2017). This protocol describes how to quantify digitized neurons into descriptive morphological features and then apply unsupervised, supervised, and statistical analysis on quantifiable morphological attributes, see also (Polavaram et al., 2014). The software setup described here was deployed on Ubuntu 20.04 LTS Linux distribution. However, all referred tools and packages function properly across different platforms, including Windows 10. We begin by illustrating how to extract quantitative morphological attributes from digital reconstructions of neurons represented in the standard SWC file format (Nanda et al., 2018). Then, we demonstrate the procedure to run unsupervised, supervised, and statistical analysis on these attributes.
